topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogen evaluation.

topics.label: Cancer Causation: Intrinsic Factors, Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer development by examining the interplay between intrinsic biological processes, genetic predispositions, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive tumorigenesis, using the interaction between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and genetic translocation in Burkitt lymphoma as a primary example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogens, Tumour Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms through which chemical and physical agents induce neoplastic transformation, including xenobiotic activation, DNA adduct formation, tumour promotion, and developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect mutational signatures and evaluate whether an agent is carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing key takeaways on carcinogenicity and framing environmental exposure within everyday risk-versus-benefit decisions.
